description: Unified education data standards graph — CEDS, SIF, Ed-Fi, PESC, CTDL, SEDM, JEDx, EdMatrix, CIP with cross-standard mappings, codeset comparison, and semantic search across all standards
_note: No startup needed. Docker --restart unless-stopped keeps containers running. First-time init: indexDataModelExplorer -start --assetsDir=./assets

definition.name: dme_search
definition.description: Semantic vector search across ALL standards in the unified graph (the live inventory comes from dme_list_standards). Vector-only — the graph carries a single vector index on :ForgedNode(embedding) and no fulltext/BM25 index. Returns results ranked by cosine relevance. Accepts optional --standard parameter to scope to a single standard. If the result is an object carrying refusedByName, your input matched nothing valid: read its reason (and validValueList when present) and say what was refused; it is NOT "no such data".

query.description: Natural language search query — concept name, field description, or question about education data elements

standard.description: Optional: limit results to a specific standard (CEDS, SIF, EdFi, PESC, CTDL, SEDM, JEDx, EdMatrix, CIP)

definition.name: dme_graph_retriever
definition.description: Semantic search with graph context enrichment. Finds similar nodes by meaning, then traverses graph relationships to return surrounding context including cross-standard mappings, types, codesets, and reference networks. Use when you need to understand how a result connects to the rest of the data model. Each mapping list (mappingsOutgoing, crossStandardEquivalents, mappingsIncoming, instanceView.mappingsViaInstances) holds at most 20 entries shared across the four match relations (each present relation first gets up to 5) and has a companion <list>TruncatedByRelation naming how many entries of each relation were left out — report those, and never call a relation absent when it was only truncated. In crossStandardEquivalents and mappingsIncoming the entries of a relation are shared round-robin across standards, so one standard never crowds out another, and <list>TruncatedByRelationAndStandard ([{relation, standard, truncatedCount}]) names what each standard lost; never call a standard unmapped when it was only truncated. For SIF and PESC results an extra instanceView object appears (absent for all other standards): instanceTotal and instancesByGroup (the element's HAS_INSTANCE instances grouped by SIF object or PESC document section), mappingsViaInstances (the element's CEDS mappings, which live on those instances, with instanceGroupList/instanceCount), instanceOf (when the node is itself an instance), and SIF structure — ownedFields/owningObjects (HAS_FIELD: object has field) and structuralParents/structuralChildren (HAS_CHILD: element contains element). For SIF and PESC, mappingsOutgoing is normally empty: read mappingsViaInstances instead. If the result is an object with retrievalMode "flat" (and a retrievalNote) instead of a list, traversal.cypher was not available and its rows carry no graph context: tell the user so, quoting the retrievalNote. If the result is an object carrying refusedByName, your input matched nothing valid: read its reason (and validValueList when present) and say what was refused; it is NOT "no such data".

query.description: Natural language description of what to search for

searchMode.description: Both values run the graph's one vector index (there is no fulltext index, so no BM25 leg); any other value is refused.

Accepts optional --standard parameter to scope to a specific standard (CEDS, SIF, EdFi, PESC, CTDL, SEDM, JEDx, EdMatrix, CIP). If the result is an object carrying refusedByName, your input matched nothing valid: read its reason (and validValueList when present) and say what was refused; it is NOT "no such data".

name.description: The exact name of the node to explore

standard.description: Optional: limit to a specific standard (CEDS, SIF, EdFi, PESC, CTDL, SEDM, JEDx, EdMatrix, CIP)

definition.name: dme_find_mappings
definition.description: Given an element from any standard, return the CEDS concept it maps to and its cross-standard equivalents. Each element resolves to a CEDS tuple — a HubReference, the canonical CEDS address — through one of four match edges, one per SKOS relation: EXACT_MATCH (same meaning), CLOSE_MATCH (near, not interchangeable), BROAD_MATCH (the CEDS tuple is broader than the element), NARROW_MATCH (the CEDS tuple is narrower). EVERY match edge is a JUDGMENT, not a fact: every row carries mappingConfidence (the judge's confidence; null on authored edges), mappingKind ('inferred' = a judge chose it, 'authored' = a document named it) and mappingSource (who decided, naming the actual judge, e.g. 'bridge-jev'; 'bridge-debug' = a DEBUG judge's mechanical placeholder, confidence 0 — if any row has it, say so first and prominently and never present it as a mapping), plus viaMappingConfidence/viaMappingKind/viaMappingSource for the queried element's hop (all null on graphs built before these fields); the relation (mappingType) and the confidence are independent — never present any row as authoritative or authored unless its mappingKind is 'authored'. Elements from different standards that resolve to the SAME HubReference form a shared-hub pair, labeled CONSERVATIVELY: direction 'equivalent' ONLY when BOTH hops are EXACT_MATCH (an equivalence composed from two judgments, not an established fact); 'candidateEquivalent' when the hops are EXACT/CLOSE with at least one CLOSE (a hypothesis); 'related' when either hop is BROAD_MATCH or NARROW_MATCH (never equivalent: both may be narrower than one broad tuple). EXACT/CLOSE rows sort first. Directions: 'outgoing' = this element's CEDS concept; 'equivalent'/'candidateEquivalent'/'related' = other standards' elements on the same concept; 'incoming' = when given a CEDS name, the source elements that map to it. Shared-hub rows carry BOTH hops' evidence: mappingType/confidence/matchPredicate/mappingConfidence/mappingSource = the other element's hop, viaMatchType/viaConfidence/viaPredicate/viaMappingConfidence/viaMappingSource = the queried element's own hop; no combined score is computed — judge from both. RETURNS AN OBJECT: mappingRowList (at most 30 rows; every relation present first gets up to 7 rows, then the rest fill composing-first by confidence, so no relation is ever dropped; WITHIN a relation the rows are shared round-robin across the source standards, best confidence first within each, so one standard never crowds out another), totalRowCountByRelation and truncatedRowCountByRelation (rows of each relation NOT shown), and totalRowCountByRelationAndStandard and truncatedRowCountByRelationAndStandard (the same, per relation and per source standard). When a truncated count is non-zero, say how many rows of that relation (and which standards' rows) were left out and offer to narrow the query; never say a relation or a standard has no mapping when its total is non-zero. Every row includes the decomposed CEDS tuple (cedsTuple: domain · property · range [· value] + canonicalKey). Accepts an element name, XPath, _id, or CEDS property name/ID. CLASSIFICATION_CROSSWALK edges (present only in graphs holding SOC and CIP) are deliberately excluded: a classification-crosswalk correspondence is not a mapping. INSTANCE NODES (SIF, PESC): these standards put their mappings on INSTANCE nodes reached by HAS_INSTANCE — a SIF Question has one Field per object it appears in; a PESC element declaration has one occurrence per place it appears in the document. Direction 'outgoingViaInstance' = the queried declaration's CEDS concept as carried by its instances, one row per CEDS tuple and verdict, with instanceGroupList (the SIF objects or PESC document sections holding it) and instanceCount (how many instances carry it). On a shared-hub or incoming row, instanceGroupList/instanceCount describe the from-element's instances that carry the mapping, and viaInstanceGroupList/viaInstanceCount describe the queried declaration's instances that carry the near hop. instanceOf names the declaration when the row's element is itself an instance. These fields are ABSENT (not null) on rows that involve no instances — CEDS, Ed-Fi and every other standard. Present instance mappings grouped by object (SIF) or section (PESC), never as repeated rows. If the result is an object carrying refusedByName, your input matched nothing valid: read its reason (and validValueList when present) and say what was refused; it is NOT "no such data".

name.description: SIF field name, XPath, CEDS property name, or CEDS ID (e.g., 'BirthDate', '/StudentPersonals/StudentPersonal/Name/FirstName', 'P600559')

definition.name: dme_compare_codesets
definition.description: Compare a codeset's allowed values across standards via the equivalence model: each source option value resolves to a value-tier CEDS hub; values from other standards on the same hub are its cross-standard equivalents. Returns one row PER VALUE — sourceValue, matchType (EXACT_MATCH / CLOSE_MATCH / BROAD_MATCH / NARROW_MATCH / null when unmatched), confidence (plus mappingConfidence, mappingKind and mappingSource when the graph records them — every match is a judgment; mappingSource 'bridge-debug' marks a debug placeholder), the CEDS value and key, and the list of other standards' values on the same CEDS value (equivalent only when both are EXACT_MATCH). Unmatched values (matchType null) show where a codeset does not align to CEDS. It does NOT compute alignment types or coverage percentages. If the result is an object carrying refusedByName, your input matched nothing valid: read its reason (and validValueList when present) and say what was refused; it is NOT "no such data".

name.description: Concept name to compare codesets for (e.g., 'grade', 'sex', 'state')

The annotation backlog. Shows standard, element name, path, and description. definition.name: dme_stats
definition.description: Whole-graph statistics across ALL loaded standards: node counts by standard (_source), node counts by universal-contract role, match-edge counts per relation (EXACT_MATCH, CLOSE_MATCH, BROAD_MATCH, NARROW_MATCH), and property-tier mapping coverage (a property counts as mapped under any of the four). For the per-standard registry list, use dme_list_standards. A SIF Question or PESC element counts as a mapped property when one of its HAS_INSTANCE instances carries the mapping edge. definition.name: dme_list_standards
definition.description: Inventory of every standard loaded in the graph. Reads the :DmeStandardRoot passport nodes and returns each standard's source, name, standardName, description, version, sourceUrl, and live nodeCount. Use this for any 'what standards are loaded?' question — it never goes stale as new standards are forged in. If the result is an object carrying refusedByName, your input matched nothing valid: read its reason (and validValueList when present) and say what was refused; it is NOT "no such data".

definition.name: dme_describe_graph
definition.description: The graph's self-description card: what this graph IS, how it was built, from what, and what it can do — read entirely from in-graph self-documentation nodes. Returns the enriched :GraphProvenance passport (build facts, capability flags, per-standard breakdown, human description), the :ManifestRecipe + :RecipeBlock recipe (every content-addressed block the graph was replayed from, with versions and purposes), the manifest ancestry (BASED_ON lineage), and one :StandardDefinition per standard (display name, version + versionSource, source format, element counts, mapping disposition authored/inferred/island). Includes a pre-rendered human 'card' field. Use this FIRST for any 'what is this graph / how was it built / what version of X is loaded?' question. Degrades honestly on graphs built before self-documentation (says what is absent). Read-only. If the result is an object carrying refusedByName, your input matched nothing valid: read its reason (and validValueList when present) and say what was refused; it is NOT "no such data".

limit.description: Maximum recipe blocks to include in the card (default 200; truncation is reported)

definition.name: dme_raw_cypher
definition.description: Execute raw Cypher against the unified graph. All nodes are :ForgedNode with a _source property indicating the standard (e.g. CEDS, EdFi, LIF); the inventory grows over time, so read _source rather than assuming a fixed list. Cross-standard mapping: a source :ForgedNode connects to a :HubReference — the canonical CEDS tuple, keyed by canonicalKey — through one of four match edges, one per SKOS relation: EXACT_MATCH, CLOSE_MATCH, BROAD_MATCH (CEDS broader), NARROW_MATCH (CEDS narrower). Every match edge is a judgment carrying predicate, confidence and, on current graphs, mappingConfidence / mappingKind ('inferred' | 'authored') / mappingSource ('bridge-<judge>', 'crosswalk-<name>', 'standard-<name>'); a judged edge is not fact, and relation and confidence are independent. Match edges carry no provenanceTier: detect debug edges by mappingSource = 'bridge-debug'. Read them with [m:EXACT_MATCH|CLOSE_MATCH|BROAD_MATCH|NARROW_MATCH]. A HubReference decomposes to its CEDS leaves via HAS_CEDS_DOMAIN, HAS_CEDS_PROPERTY, HAS_CEDS_RANGE, HAS_CEDS_VALUE, HAS_CEDS_QUALIFIER. Two source elements sharing a HubReference are equivalent only when both hops are EXACT_MATCH (two judgments); a CLOSE hop makes them a candidate; a BROAD/NARROW hop makes them only related. Graphs holding SOC and CIP also link them by CLASSIFICATION_CROSSWALK edges (NCES crosswalk; NOT equivalence — never compose them with match-edge hub resolutions). INSTANCE NODES: SIF and PESC carry mappings on instances, not on the element search finds — (decl:ForgedNode {role:'DmeProperty'})-[:HAS_INSTANCE]->(inst:ForgedNode {role:'DmeSupport'})-[:EXACT_MATCH|CLOSE_MATCH|BROAD_MATCH|NARROW_MATCH]->(:HubReference). A SIF instance's group is its owning Object, (obj)-[:HAS_FIELD]->(inst); a PESC instance's group is inst.sectionPath. SIF nesting: Object -[:HAS_CHILD]-> Container -[:HAS_CHILD]-> Container|Field. If the result is an object carrying refusedByName, your input matched nothing valid: read its reason (and validValueList when present) and say what was refused; it is NOT "no such data".
